chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man and woman who perform Tamattu' (Umrah followed by Hajj) and then enter Mecca on the Day of Arafah; what should they do? He said: 'They make it a single Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad), and the limit of Tamattu' is until the Day of Tarwiyah.'

key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of Arafah (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who enters Mecca on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the procedural nuance for those performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who enter Mecca on the Day of Arafah, ruling that their Umrah and Hajj are consolidated into a single Hajj al-Mufrad. This ruling highlights the flexibility in the timing of Ihram renewal, specifying that the boundary for the Umrah portion extends until the Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah), ensuring the pilgrim's rites remain valid despite the delayed entry. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for defining the precise temporal limits of ritual states during the Hajj season.
